gloss: Three visits to a thatched cottage; shows great respect and determination to recruit talent.
teaser: Ever wondered how persistence can lead to greatness?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how persistence can lead to greatness? [break 1s] The phrase is: 三顾茅庐, sān gù máo lú. [break 1s] 三 (sān) - three [break 0.5s] 顾 (gù) - visit [break 0.5s] 茅 (máo) - thatched [break 0.5s] 庐 (lú) - cottage [break 1s] The full idiom again: 三顾茅庐 means 'three visits to a thatched cottage'. Literally, it describes someone who visits multiple times to seek assistance, figuratively highlighting the importance of perseverance in recruiting talent. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] During the Three Kingdoms period, the warlord Liu Bei was eager to recruit the brilliant strategist Zhuge Liang. Liu Bei made three trips to Zhuge Liang's humble abode, demonstrating his determination and respect. This persistence eventually paid off, as Zhuge Liang became one of Liu Bei's most trusted advisors. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他为了找到合适的人才，三顾茅庐。 He made three visits to recruit the right talent. [break 1s] Example 2: 老板为了请到这个专家，真是三顾茅庐。 The boss really went out of his way to recruit this expert. [break 1s] Example 3: 在求学的路上，我们都需要三顾茅庐的精神。 On the path of learning, we all need the spirit of persistence. [break 1s] So, that’s 三顾茅庐, which means to show great respect and determination in seeking talent. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
